subject: evaluating an expression inside a ggplot2 layer expression

messages.author: 91843c5602a10b9b
messages.subject: evaluating an expression inside a ggplot2 layer expression
parts:
Hello,

I would like to produce a graph showing simulatenously logs with a
bunch of bases. The following does not work because the "i" in the
aesthetic of the geom_point never gets evaluated:

x<-seq(0,100,1)

y<-log(x,base=exp(1))
logs<-ggplot(data.frame(x,y),aes(x=x,y=y))
for(i in 2:10) {
logs<-logs + (geom_point(aes(y=log(x,base=i))))
}

this does not return an error, but if you put summary(logs), you will
see that the "i" is left unevaluated so that it will only plot one
logarithm, the one of the current value of i.

I am interested in alternative ways to do this, but I am also very
curious to know how to force R or ggplot to evaluate the i during the
loop.

Thank you,

Xu Wang

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: evaluating an expression inside a ggplot2 layer expression
parts:
Hi Xu,

I'd do something like this:

eval(substitute(geom_point(aes(y=log(x,base=i))), list(i = 1)))

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: evaluating an expression inside a ggplot2 layer expression
parts:
Thanks Hadley!

For completeness, here is my script:

library(ggplot2)
x<-seq(0,100,1)
y<-log(x,base=exp(1))
logs<-ggplot(data.frame(x),aes(x=x))

for (i in 2:10) {
logs<-logs +
eval(substitute(geom_point(aes(y=log(x,base=j))),list(j=i)))
}

logs<-logs + geom_point(aes(y=log(x,base=exp(1))),color="red")

print(logs<-logs + ylab("log(x) using bases {2:10,e}. Base e is in
red."))
